column.text: Bitcoin is currently bleeding hard, having just dipped below $84,000 as the market digests a brutal wave of long liquidations totaling nearly half a billion dollars. The pain is acute across the board, with Ethereum taking an even steeper hit down 3.21% while spot ETFs saw a fresh $90 million outflow. This isn't just noise; it is a structural shift where extreme whale positioning on Hyperliquid reveals massive net shorts worth hundreds of millions sitting atop every major asset. Yet, beneath the red tape lies a dangerous confluence of technical exhaustion. The one-hour RSI for Bitcoin has crashed to 30.18 and Ethereum to 17.67, screaming that downside momentum is genuinely drying up. While dollar liquidity remains flat with no macro tailwinds to catch a falling knife, the crowded short positioning on BTC and SOL creates a ticking time bomb waiting for a stabilization above key support levels. A reflexive dip buy here is a recipe for getting squeezed, but a high-conviction counter-trend long at this exact exhaustion point carries significant asymmetric reward potential. The narrative has shifted from pure fear to a calculated wait for the next catalyst, whether it be a failed reclaim of the 20-day moving average or a sudden negative funding squeeze that forces shorts into the air. With Standard Chartered declaring the cycle low officially behind us at roughly $86K, the setup is primed for a volatile rebound rather than a prolonged grind lower. Traders must wait for real momentum proof before chasing breakouts, but those prepared to catch the short-squeeze wave as liquidity flows reverse will find the entry of a lifetime waiting right now in this oversold environment.
